meta.title: Architectural Estimation Rules: LGS Building System
meta.module: Architectural estimation module of the in-house estimation software
meta.summary: The software measures the surface, the estimator selects the material and then its specification for that usage location, and the software calculates the quantity, accessories, wastage and purchase units.
meta.status: Rates, sheet sizes, wastage percentages and default dimensions are typical starting defaults. They are editable master data and must be confirmed against UNIQUBE supplier data before use. See to_confirm.

conventions.formulas: Plain expressions. round_up is ceiling, round_down is floor. Areas are in m2 and lengths in m unless a name ends in _mm. Parameters stored in mm are converted to m before use.
conventions.rule_ids: Two-letter group code plus number, for example GM-08. IDs match the specification document.

terms.meaning: A usage position in the building, for example the outer face of an external wall. The list is fixed (see locations).
A layer position inside a location. Each slot is mandatory (M), conditional (C) or optional (O).
What the estimator picks for a slot, for example cement board.
The purchasable variant of a material: thickness, sheet size, pack size, supplier and rate.
One measured face or area from geometry, for example the room-side face of one wall in one room. A surface belongs to exactly one location.
DRY, WET or EXTERNAL. An attribute of a room that decides which location its surfaces fall in.
An accessory generated from a parent material by a consumption rule.
The installed quantity measured from geometry, after opening deductions and reveal additions.
Gross converted to purchase units (sheets, boxes, bags, rolls, pails) and rounded up.
The return faces around an opening: jambs, head and sill.
The level at which a selection applies: project, level, room type, wall type, room or single surface.

fields: Room on side B, or EXTERIOR
Gross area to the outer face of structure

data_model.note: Table names are suggestions; the fields are the requirement. New materials, specifications, rates and parameters are added by the administrator with no code change. A new location or slot needs a developer only when it introduces a new way of measuring.

tables.purpose: Which materials are allowed in which slot
Purchasable variants. Attributes include thickness, sheet size, density, colour and coverage.
Accessory generation. Basis is per m2, per m, per nr or formula.
Results. Source is AUTO, DEPENDENT, INPUT or OVERRIDE.

rule_constants.note: Numbers that appear inside rule texts, listed so they can be stored as master data (PR-07). Key names are suggestions.

notes: Slots are listed from outside to inside, or from bottom to top.
The outer face of a parapet is part of EW-OUT, because façade height runs to the top of the parapet.
The ground floor slab belongs to the Structure module. FL-DECK applies to upper floors only.
A mandatory slot can be set to 'Not required' only with a reason (VL-01).

External wall, inner face to a wet room

list.measured_as: Area per face: room-side length × lining height

list.measured_as: Area per face: room-side length × lining height

slot_options.note: Starting list of materials offered in each slot and the specification attributes the estimator selects. The administrator extends it.

SILL.label: External sill or internal sill board

rules.title: Usage-first selection
rules.rule: Every item is selected by usage location. The estimator picks the material for the location, then the specification of that material. The software never picks a material by itself.

rules.title: Fixed hierarchy
rules.rule: Location → Slot → Material → Specification → Quantity. A slot is one layer position inside a location, such as sheathing board, weather barrier or finish.

rules.title: Filtered lists
rules.rule: The material list shows only materials allowed in that slot. The specification list shows only specifications of the chosen material. Both lists come from master data.

rules.title: Geometry automatic, selection manual, quantity automatic
rules.rule: The estimator never types a dimension the software can measure. Where geometry cannot supply a dimension, the item becomes an estimator-input item and is flagged in the output.

rules.title: One method for all items
rules.rule: Area, length, count and volume items all follow PR-01 to PR-04. Only the measurement formula differs.

rules.title: One owner per item
rules.rule: Items quantified by the Structure module (studs, tracks, joists, trusses, bracing, lintels, structural deck, foundations) are never quantified again here. Every material carries an owner_module field.

rules.title: No hard-coded numbers
rules.rule: Every rate, sheet size, wastage percentage, threshold and default height is master data with an effective date.

rules.title: Three quantities per line
rules.rule: Net (installed), gross (net plus wastage) and purchase (gross converted to purchase units and rounded up) are all stored.

rules.title: Dependents are automatic
rules.rule: Screws, tape, compound, adhesive, grout, primer, beads, sealant and fixings are generated from the parent selection by consumption rules. The estimator does not select them.

rules.title: Traceable
rules.rule: Every quantity line stores its source surfaces, formula ID and parameter values, so a reviewer can recalculate it by hand.

rules.title: Override with reason
rules.rule: A manual change to an automatic quantity, rate or validation needs a typed reason. The automatic value is kept and the line is flagged.

rules.title: SI storage
rules.rule: Dimensions are stored in mm; quantities in m, m², m³, kg, L and nr. Imperial is a display conversion only.

rules.title: Procurement mode
rules.rule: Each material is MATERIAL (broken down into components for in-house installation) or SUPPLY_INSTALL (a subcontract package measured as one line in m², m or nr). Dependents are generated only in MATERIAL mode.
Each wall face is split at room boundaries. Every surface then faces exactly one room, or the exterior.
Zone comes from room type. Default WET: bathroom, toilet, shower, laundry, kitchen. Default EXTERNAL: balcony, terrace. All other rooms are DRY. The mapping is editable per project.
A missing field uses the project default parameter. Every line that depends on it is flagged 'assumed'.
Geometry is read-only in this module. Corrections are made in the plan reader, so Structure and Architecture stay aligned.
Opening sizes are structural opening sizes: the framed width and height.
Stud depth, stud spacing, steel thickness and joist spacing are read from the Structure module and never re-entered.

rules.title: Base formula
rules.rule: Net area of a surface = length × height − deductible openings + reveals. Board slots multiply the result by the number of layers.
rules.formula: net_area = length * height - sum(deductible_opening_areas) + sum(reveal_areas); board slots: net_area * layers

rules.title: Length
rules.rule: EW-OUT uses the outer-face length, outside corner to outside corner. Inner faces and internal wall faces use the length of the face inside the room. Cavities use the wall centreline length. If rooms are not available, use centreline length and flag the line 'assumed'.

rules.title: Façade height (EW-OUT)
rules.rule: Per storey: finished floor level to the finished floor level above, so the floor zone is covered. The ground storey starts at the top of the plinth. The top storey runs to the top of the parapet, or to the eaves on a pitched roof. Gable ends add ½ × gable width × rise.

rules.title: Lining height
rules.rule: Ceiling height + LINING_OVERRUN (default 150 mm). The lining runs the full structural panel height when the room has no ceiling, when the wall is fire or acoustic rated, or when the estimator sets full height.
rules.formula: lining_height = ceiling_height + LINING_OVERRUN; or structural_panel_height when full height applies

rules.title: Finish height
rules.rule: Paint, tiles and wall panels are measured to ceiling height only. Tiles may stop at a tiling height chosen by the estimator.

rules.title: Height bands
rules.rule: Two finishes on one face are measured as bands, for example tiles from 0 to 1200 mm and paint above. An opening is deducted from each band by its overlap: opening width × the part of its sill-to-head height that lies inside the band.
rules.formula: band_deduction = opening_width * overlap_height(sill_height to sill_height + opening_height, band_bottom to band_top)

rules.title: Cavity height
rules.rule: Structural panel (stud) height.

rules.title: Opening deduction
rules.rule: Openings larger than SMALL_OPENING_AREA (default 0.50 m²) are deducted in full. Smaller openings are not deducted, because the cut-out is waste. A material may be set to FULL or NONE instead of this default. One opening deducts from every slot on both faces of its host wall and from the cavity.
rules.formula: deduct opening_width * opening_height when opening_width * opening_height > SMALL_OPENING_AREA

rules.title: Reveals
rules.rule: Materials flagged 'returns into reveal' add reveal perimeter × reveal depth. Door: 2 × height + width. Window, outer face: 2 × (height + width). Window, inner face: 2 × height + width when a sill board is selected, otherwise 2 × (height + width). Depths are REVEAL_DEPTH_EXT and REVEAL_DEPTH_INT (default 100 mm each).
rules.formula: reveal_area = reveal_perimeter * reveal_depth; door: 2 * height + width; window outer face: 2 * (height + width); window inner face: 2 * height + width if sill board selected, else 2 * (height + width)

rules.title: Floors
rules.rule: Finish area = room net floor area + door strips. Each door adds door width × half the wall thickness to the room on each side. Deck area = gross floor plate less stair voids and shafts.
rules.formula: finish_area = room_net_floor_area + sum(door_width * wall_thickness / 2); deck_area = gross_floor_plate - stair_voids - shafts

rules.title: Ceilings
rules.rule: Area = room net floor area. Bulkhead and drop faces add length × drop height, as estimator input unless read from a ceiling plan.

rules.title: Slopes
rules.rule: True area = plan area ÷ cos(slope).

rules.title: Lengths
rules.rule: Skirting = room perimeter − door widths. Cornice and shadow gap = room perimeter. Copings and flashings = measured edge length.

rules.title: Order
rules.rule: Net, then dependents from net, then wastage, then purchase conversion, then rounding. Intermediate values keep four decimals. Only the purchase quantity is rounded, always up.

rules.title: Aggregation
rules.rule: Purchase rounding is applied once per specification per lot. The lot is the whole project by default, or one level when the project is delivered by level.

rules.title: Data errors
rules.rule: If deductions exceed the gross area, or an opening does not fit its host wall, the line stops with an error. It is never set to zero silently.
Net board area per slot = sum of surface areas (GM-01) × layers. Each layer may have its own material and specification.
Sheets = round up [ net × (1 + wastage) ÷ (sheet length × sheet width) ].

rules.title: Height fit
rules.rule: When board height H is not more than sheet length Ls, the surface uses wastage = the larger of the default wastage and (Ls ÷ H − 1 + 3%). The software then suggests the stock length closest above H. When H is more than Ls, the default wastage applies.
rules.formula: if H <= Ls: wastage = max(default_wastage, Ls / H - 1 + 0.03); else: wastage = default_wastage

rules.title: Screws
rules.rule: Quantity per layer = net area × the rate from DP-01, using the stud or joist spacing from the Structure module.

rules.title: Screw selection
rules.rule: Length = the shortest stocked length not less than the total board thickness being fixed + 10 mm. Point = drill point when the stud steel is thicker than DRILL_POINT_STEEL (default 0.7 mm), otherwise sharp point.
rules.formula: screw_length_mm = min(stocked_length_mm where stocked_length_mm >= total_board_thickness_mm + 10); point = drill if stud_steel_thickness_mm > DRILL_POINT_STEEL else sharp

rules.title: Jointing, gypsum
rules.rule: Tape and compound apply to the face layer only. Inner layers of a multi-layer lining are not taped unless the fire system requires it.

rules.title: Corner beads
rules.rule: Length = convex corners in the room × lining height + reveal perimeters of the openings on that face (GM-09). If corner counts are not read, use 0.30 m per m² of board and flag 'assumed'.
rules.formula: bead_length = convex_corners * lining_height + sum(reveal_perimeters); fallback: 0.30 * board_area

rules.title: External cement board
rules.rule: Board joints take joint filler and alkali-resistant tape. The render system supplies the remaining layers (EF-02).

rules.title: Floor cement board
rules.rule: Area = FL-DECK area. Sheets are laid with the long edge across the joists. A construction adhesive bead runs on every joist: length = area ÷ joist spacing.

rules.title: Glass mat sheathing
rules.rule: If the product is used as the weather barrier with sealed joints, the WRB slot is set to 'integrated' and the joint sealant becomes a dependent of the board.

rules.title: Weather barrier
rules.rule: Net area = EW-OUT sheathing net area, reveals included. Laps are covered by 15% wastage. Rolls = round up (gross ÷ roll area).

rules.title: Vapour control layer
rules.rule: Net area = cavity net area of the wall. Laps are covered by 10% wastage. The slot is mandatory for cold-climate profiles and optional for GCC profiles. Its position in the wall is a design decision; the software only quantifies it.

rules.title: Cavity insulation
rules.rule: Net area = centreline length × stud height − openings (GM-08). Studs are not deducted. Packs = round up (gross ÷ m² per pack).
rules.formula: net_area = centreline_length * stud_height - sum(deductible_opening_areas); packs = round_up(gross / m2_per_pack)

rules.title: Floor, ceiling and roof insulation
rules.rule: Net area = floor plate, ceiling or roof area. Same pack rule.

rules.title: External insulation
rules.rule: Net area = EW-OUT net area. Adhesive and mechanical fixings come from the system data sheet (default 6 fixings per m²).

rules.title: Wet-room waterproofing
rules.rule: Area = room floor area + room perimeter × WP_UPTURN (default 300 mm) + shower wall length × WP_SHOWER_HEIGHT (default 2100 mm). Shower wall length is read from the plan if the fixture is recognised, otherwise entered per room type. Quantity = area × consumption for all coats, from the specification.
rules.formula: area = room_floor_area + room_perimeter * WP_UPTURN + shower_wall_length * WP_SHOWER_HEIGHT; quantity = area * consumption

rules.title: Roof and terrace waterproofing
rules.rule: Area = plan area + parapet length × WP_UPSTAND (default 300 mm) + upstands to plinths and penetrations (RF-07). Sheet membranes carry 15% wastage for laps. Liquid systems use consumption × area.
rules.formula: area = plan_area + parapet_length * WP_UPSTAND + sum(penetration_perimeter * WP_UPSTAND)

rules.title: Waterproofing accessories
rules.rule: Primer by area. Reinforcing tape = room perimeter + number of wall corners × upturn height. Roofs add an angle fillet and a termination bar, each equal to the parapet length.

rules.title: Sill gasket
rules.rule: Length under ground-floor base tracks = total ground-floor wall centreline length − door widths. Width follows stud depth.

rules.title: Perimeter sealant on rated walls
rules.rule: Bead length = 2 faces × 2 × (wall length + lining height). Cartridges follow DP-06.
Finish area = EW-OUT net area including reveals (GM-01). Parapet inner faces and soffits are measured in their own locations.

rules.title: Textured render system (Terraco or equivalent)
rules.rule: One selection generates primer, basecoat, reinforcing mesh and finish coat. Consumption comes from the system data sheet. The finish coat rate varies with grain size and is stored on the specification.

rules.title: Render beads
rules.rule: Corner bead = building convex corners × façade height + reveal perimeters. Drip bead = total width of window and door heads. Base bead = external perimeter − external door widths. Movement bead = one horizontal run per intermediate floor line, plus vertical joints at MJ_SPACING (default 6 m). Vertical joints per elevation = round down (elevation length ÷ spacing), each as long as the façade height.
rules.formula: corner_bead = building_convex_corners * facade_height + sum(reveal_perimeters); drip_bead = sum(opening_head_widths); base_bead = external_perimeter - sum(external_door_widths); vertical_joints_per_elevation = round_down(elevation_length / MJ_SPACING)

rules.title: Exterior paint
rules.rule: Litres = area × coats ÷ coverage. Coverage on textured surfaces is lower than on smooth ones and is stored on the specification.

rules.title: Mixed finishes
rules.rule: Finishes are assigned per surface (elevation or wall segment). Where the split does not follow wall segments, the estimator enters the area of the second finish and the software deducts it from the first.

rules.title: ACP as SUPPLY_INSTALL
rules.rule: One line in m² of finished area, reveals and returns included, plus copings and flashings by length.

rules.title: ACP as MATERIAL
rules.rule: Sheets = round up [ net × (1 + wastage) ÷ sheet area ], with default wastage 20% for cassette returns and module cutting. Subframe rail length = area ÷ rail spacing (default 600 mm). Brackets = rail length ÷ bracket spacing (default 1.0 m). Joint sealant and backer rod length = area × (panel width + panel height) ÷ (panel width × panel height). The panel module is a specification input.
rules.formula: sheets = round_up(net * (1 + wastage) / sheet_area); rail_length = area / rail_spacing; brackets = rail_length / bracket_spacing; joint_length = area * (panel_width + panel_height) / (panel_width * panel_height)

rules.title: ACP fire grade
rules.rule: Every ACP specification must carry a fire classification accepted by the fire code that applies to the project; in the UAE, the Fire and Life Safety Code. A specification without one cannot be selected.

rules.title: Plank and panel cladding
rules.rule: Area with 10% wastage. Support rail length = area ÷ rail spacing. Corner, starter and opening trims by length. Fixings per m² from the specification.
Floor tile net area = floor finish area (GM-10). Wall tile net area = room perimeter × tiling height − openings + reveals + niches entered by the estimator.
rules.formula: wall_tile_net = room_perimeter * tiling_height - sum(deductible_opening_areas) + sum(reveal_areas) + niches

rules.title: Wastage by layout
rules.rule: Straight lay with tile sides under 900 mm: 8%. Large format, any side 900 mm or more: 10%. Diagonal or herringbone: 15%.
Boxes = round up (gross ÷ m² per box). Attic stock (ATTIC_STOCK, default 0%) is added to the purchase quantity and shown separately.

rules.title: Adhesive
rules.rule: Net area × rate by longest tile side: up to 300 mm, 3.5 kg/m²; 301 to 600 mm, 5.0 kg/m²; over 600 mm, 7.0 kg/m².

rules.title: Grout
rules.rule: kg per m² = (L + W) ÷ (L × W) × joint width × joint depth × 1.6, with tile length L, tile width W, joint width and joint depth all in mm.

rules.title: Trims
rules.rule: External tile corners × tiling height, plus the top edge of the tiling where it stops below the ceiling (room perimeter − door widths).

rules.title: Skirting
rules.rule: Length per GM-13. Not generated on faces tiled down to the floor. If skirting is cut from floor tiles, add skirting length × skirting height × 1.15 to the floor tile area instead.

rules.title: Thresholds and transition strips
rules.rule: One per door into a wet room, and one per door where the floor finish changes. Length = door width.

rules.title: Screed
rules.rule: Volume = area × thickness. Bagged products: kg = area × thickness in mm × 2.0 for sand-cement, or × 1.7 for self-levelling compound. Screed to falls: average thickness = minimum thickness + fall × longest run ÷ 2.
rules.formula: volume = area * thickness; bagged_kg = area * thickness_mm * 2.0 (sand-cement) or * 1.7 (self-levelling); average_thickness = minimum_thickness + fall * longest_run / 2

rules.title: Plank floors (SPC, laminate)
rules.rule: Boxes from area with 8% wastage. Underlay = net area × 1.05.

rules.title: Metal deck with concrete topping
rules.rule: Applies when the deck is not owned by the Structure module. Deck area = floor plate × 1.05. Concrete volume = area × (topping above ribs + rib depth × rib fill factor, default 0.5). Mesh = area × 1.15. Edge trim = floor plate perimeter + void perimeters.
rules.formula: deck_area = floor_plate * 1.05; concrete_volume = area * (topping_above_ribs + rib_depth * rib_fill_factor); mesh = area * 1.15; edge_trim = floor_plate_perimeter + sum(void_perimeters)

rules.title: Paint to an exposed deck soffit
rules.rule: Area = plan area × the profile factor from the deck specification (default 1.4).

rules.title: Stairs
rules.rule: Tread finish = treads × width × (going + nosing). Riser finish = risers × width × rise. Landings by area. Nosing strips = treads × width.
rules.formula: tread_finish = treads * width * (going + nosing); riser_finish = risers * width * rise; nosing_strips = treads * width

rules.rule: Ceiling area per GM-11. Lights, diffusers and hatches under 0.50 m² are not deducted.

rules.title: Gypsum board ceilings
rules.rule: Boards per BD-02 with 10% wastage. The face layer is taped (BD-06).

rules.title: Fixing type
rules.rule: A specification attribute: DIRECT_FIX (furring channels screwed under the joists or trusses) or SUSPENDED (hangers, primary channels and furring channels).

rules.title: Framing
rules.rule: Furring length = area ÷ furring spacing. Primary channel length = area ÷ primary spacing. Hangers = area ÷ (primary spacing × hanger spacing), with one anchor each. Connecting clips = area ÷ (primary spacing × furring spacing). Perimeter channel = room perimeter. Primary channels, hangers and clips apply to SUSPENDED only. Default spacings: furring 400 mm, primary 1200 mm, hangers 1200 mm.
rules.formula: furring_length = area / furring_spacing; primary_length = area / primary_spacing; hangers = area / (primary_spacing * hanger_spacing); clips = area / (primary_spacing * furring_spacing); perimeter_channel = room_perimeter

rules.title: Metal tile, lay-in 600 × 600
rules.rule: Tiles = round up [ area × 1.05 ÷ tile area ]. Main tee length = area ÷ 1.2. Cross tee 1200 length = area ÷ 0.6. Cross tee 600 length = area ÷ 1.2. Wall angle = room perimeter. Hangers = area ÷ 1.44.
rules.formula: tiles = round_up(area * 1.05 / tile_area); main_tee = area / 1.2; cross_tee_1200 = area / 0.6; cross_tee_600 = area / 1.2; wall_angle = room_perimeter; hangers = area / 1.44

rules.title: Metal tile, clip-in
rules.rule: Carrier length = area ÷ tile module. Primary channel length = area ÷ 1.2. Hangers as CL-05.
rules.formula: carrier_length = area / tile_module; primary_length = area / 1.2; hangers = area / 1.44

rules.title: Metal strip
rules.rule: Strip length = area ÷ strip module. Carrier length = area ÷ carrier spacing (default 1.2 m). Edge profile = room perimeter.
rules.formula: strip_length = area / strip_module; carrier_length = area / carrier_spacing; edge_profile = room_perimeter

rules.title: Bulkheads and drops
rules.rule: Board and framing by face area. One corner bead per exposed edge.

rules.title: Access panels
rules.rule: The count is estimator input, with a default of one per wet room and one per concealed AC unit.

rules.title: External soffit
rules.rule: Exterior-grade board on framing per CL-04. Finish per the external finish rules.

rules.title: Ceiling paint
rules.rule: Litres = ceiling area × coats ÷ coverage.
True roof area = plan area ÷ cos(slope), overhangs included.

rules.title: Pitched cover
rules.rule: Sandwich panels and profiled sheets = true area × 1.05. Optional refinement: sheets per slope = round up (eaves length ÷ cover width), each as long as the rafter plus the overhang.
rules.formula: cover_area = true_area * 1.05; optional: sheets_per_slope = round_up(eaves_length / cover_width)

rules.title: Pitched accessories
rules.rule: Ridge cap = ridge length. Eaves flashing = eaves length. Barge flashing = verge length. Each carries 10% for laps. Fixings per m² come from the specification.

rules.title: Gutters and downpipes
rules.rule: Gutter length = eaves length. The downpipe count is estimator input; the software suggests round up (plan area ÷ DP_AREA), minimum 2, with DP_AREA at 80 m² until MEP confirms. Downpipe length = count × (eaves height + 0.5 m).
rules.formula: suggested_downpipes = max(2, round_up(plan_area / DP_AREA)); downpipe_length = count * (eaves_height + 0.5)

rules.title: Flat roof build-up
rules.rule: Deck per BD-09 or TF-11. Insulation boards = area × 1.05. Screed to falls per TF-09. Waterproofing per IN-07. Protection layer by area.

rules.title: Parapet
rules.rule: Inner face area = parapet length × parapet height, with sheathing, weather barrier and finish as for an external wall. Coping = parapet length × 1.05, with corners and stop ends by count.

rules.title: Penetrations and plinths
rules.rule: AC units, tanks, hatches and skylights. The count is estimator input. Each adds waterproofing = its perimeter × WP_UPSTAND.
Trusses, purlins and structural deck belong to the Structure module (PR-06).
Count by type mark from the opening schedule. Each type holds width, height, usage (external, internal, wet room, fire rated) and configuration.

rules.title: Doorset
rules.rule: The estimator selects material, configuration, fire rating and finish per door type. One doorset = leaf or leaves + frame.

rules.title: Frame depth
rules.rule: Finished wall thickness = stud depth + all board thicknesses on both faces + 15 mm per tiled face. The software calculates it from the wall selections and offers only matching frame depths.

rules.title: Ironmongery
rules.rule: Selected as one set per door function. The set defines its own items: hinges (3 per leaf up to 2.1 m high; 4 above that or on fire doors), lock or latch, handles, door stop, and closer and seals on fire doors. Double doors add 2 flush bolts to the inactive leaf.

rules.title: Door surround
rules.rule: Architrave = (2 × height + width) × faces with architrave × 1.10. Perimeter sealant = (2 × height + width) × 2 faces. Frame fixings = 8 per frame. External doors add one threshold with weather seal.
rules.formula: architrave = (2 * height + width) * faces_with_architrave * 1.10; perimeter_sealant = (2 * height + width) * 2; frame_fixings = 8

rules.title: Windows
rules.rule: Count by type mark; area (width × height) is stored for m² pricing. The specification holds system, opening type, glazing and finish.

rules.title: Window surround
rules.rule: Per window of width W and height H. Flashing tape = 2 × (W + H) + 0.6 m. External sealant with backer rod = 2 × (W + H). Internal sealant = 2 × (W + H). Fixing anchors = round up [ 2 × (W + H) ÷ 0.6 ]. External sill, internal sill board and head flashing = W + 0.1 m each, when selected.
rules.formula: flashing_tape = 2 * (W + H) + 0.6; external_sealant = 2 * (W + H); internal_sealant = 2 * (W + H); anchors = round_up(2 * (W + H) / 0.6); sill = W + 0.1

rules.title: Safety glazing
rules.rule: Glazing in doors, in panels beside doors, and in windows with a sill below SAFETY_SILL (default 800 mm) needs a tempered or laminated specification.

rules.title: Curtain wall, shopfronts and louvres
rules.rule: Area per type, as SUPPLY_INSTALL.
Every opening applies GM-08 and GM-09 to its host wall automatically. Lintels and trimmers belong to the Structure module.

rules.title: Fixture backing
rules.rule: Plywood or steel plate inside stud walls. Wall cabinets: 2 rows × cabinet run. One plate each for wash basin, wall-hung WC, grab bar, TV point and AC indoor unit. Counts default by room type and are flagged 'assumed'.

rules.title: Fire stopping
rules.rule: Head-of-wall sealant = fire-rated wall length × 2 faces. Penetration seals = count from the MEP module when available, otherwise estimator input.

rules.title: Control joints in linings
rules.rule: Joints per wall run = round down (run length ÷ CJ_SPACING, default 9 m). Length = count × lining height.
rules.formula: joints = round_down(run_length / CJ_SPACING); length = joints * lining_height

rules.title: Boxing and pipe casings
rules.rule: Board and framing = length × girth, as estimator input.

rules.title: Joinery and fitments
rules.rule: Kitchen base units, wall units and countertops by length; splashback by area; wardrobes by front area or count; vanity units, mirrors and shower enclosures by count; one sanitary accessory set per bathroom.

rules.title: Sanitaryware
rules.rule: WC, basin and mixers belong to the MEP module (PR-06).

rules.title: Balustrades and handrails
rules.rule: Length from stair geometry and from balcony and terrace edges. Posts = round up (length ÷ post spacing) + 1.

rules.title: Canopies, pergolas, signage and screens
rules.rule: Estimator input by count or area.
Scaffolding, protection, cleaning and site attendance are preliminaries and sit outside this module.

rules.title: Screw rate
rules.rule: Screws per sheet = (round down [ sheet dimension across the supports ÷ support spacing ] + 1) × (round down [ sheet dimension along the supports ÷ screw spacing ] + 1). Rate per m² = screws per sheet ÷ sheet area, rounded up to a whole number. On walls the sheet width runs across the studs. On ceilings and floors the sheet length runs across the supports.
rules.formula: screws_per_sheet = (round_down(dimension_across_supports / support_spacing) + 1) * (round_down(dimension_along_supports / screw_spacing) + 1); rate_per_m2 = round_up(screws_per_sheet / sheet_area)

rules.rule: Dependents are calculated from the parent's net quantity, then take their own wastage.
A dependent never generates further dependents. Conversions such as bead length to cartridges are purchase conversions.
A rule may carry a condition: face layer only, a stud spacing, a zone, or MATERIAL mode only.
The same dependent from several parents is summed into one purchase line per specification. Parent links are kept for tracing.

rules.title: Sealant
rules.rule: Metres per cartridge = cartridge volume in ml ÷ (bead width × bead depth in mm). A 600 ml pack at 10 × 5 mm gives 12 m.
Gross = net × (1 + wastage). Wastage comes from the material group, unless the specification, the project or a rule (BD-03, TF-02) sets another value.
Purchase quantity = round up (gross ÷ base units per purchase unit). Examples of the divisor: m² per sheet, m² per box, kg per bag, L per pail, m per length, nr per box.
Linear stock: pieces = round up (gross length ÷ stock length). Cutting optimisation is not part of version 1.
If the purchase quantity is below the supplier's minimum order, show the minimum order quantity and flag the line.
Version 1 uses one pack size per specification.

rule_groups.name: Validation rules
rule_groups.note: Errors stop the estimate from being issued. Warnings need the estimator's acknowledgement.

rules.rule: Every mandatory slot of every location present in the project has a selection, or 'Not required' with a reason.

Conditional slots are filled when their condition is true: cavity insulation in acoustic or fire-rated walls; waterproofing to shower walls; roof insulation under a single-skin cover; VCL in cold-climate profiles.
Linings and ceilings facing a wet room are MR gypsum, FR-MR gypsum, cement board or glass mat tile backer.
Linings on a fire-rated wall meet the minimum build-up in the fire table for that rating.
Materials in EW-OUT, PAR, CL-EXT and FL-EXT are flagged exterior grade.
Cavity insulation thickness is not more than the stud depth.
Every ACP specification carries a fire classification (EF-08).
Every room has a room type and zone. Every wall face is assigned to a room or to the exterior.
Room areas on a level do not exceed the floor plate area. Every opening fits its host wall.
A material owned by another module cannot be selected (PR-06).
A specification used in pricing has a valid unit rate and pack size.
Door frame depth matches the finished wall thickness within 5 mm (DW-03).
Safety glazing is selected where DW-08 requires it.
Sheet length suits the board height (BD-03).
A stocked screw length exists for the lining thickness (BD-05).
Lines that use assumed values are counted on the summary.
A template stores a full set of selections by location and slot, for example a standard villa build-up. Applying it fills the selections; the estimator can change any of them.
Templates are versioned. A project records the template name and version it started from.

rules.title: Scope precedence
rules.rule: The most specific selection wins: surface, then room, then wall type, then room type, then level, then project default.
Selections can be copied from one level or room type to another.
An override can change a quantity, a wastage percentage or a dependent rate, or waive a validation. It needs a reason, keeps the automatic value and is flagged in the output.
A change to geometry, selection or master data marks the affected lines stale and recalculates them. An override is flagged for review if its automatic value moved by more than 5%.
Master data is effective-dated. An issued estimate is frozen with the rates and rules in force on its issue date.
Three roles: estimator (selects and overrides), reviewer (approves overrides and waivers), administrator (maintains master data and templates).

rule_groups.name: Outputs
rule_groups.note: The calculation steps are listed in calculation_sequence.

rules.title: Bill of quantities
rules.rule: By trade, location and specification: net, wastage, gross, purchase quantity, unit, rate, amount.

rules.title: Procurement list
rules.rule: One line per specification with purchase quantity and supplier, split by lot.

rules.title: Room data sheet
rules.rule: The selected build-up and finishes for each room.

rules.title: Exceptions report
rules.rule: Assumed values, overrides, waivers and warnings.

rules.title: Trace view
rules.rule: From any quantity to its surfaces, dimensions, formula ID and parameters.

calculation_sequence.action: Load geometry, build surfaces and assign each surface to a location.
Resolve the selection for every surface and slot by scope precedence.
Run validations. Errors stop the run; warnings continue.
Calculate the net quantity per surface and slot, using the GM rules and the rules of each material family.
Generate dependents from the net quantities.
Apply wastage to get gross quantities.
Aggregate by specification and lot, convert to purchase units and round up.
Price each line: purchase quantity × unit rate.
Write the quantity lines with their trace data.

screw_rates.note: Rates at common spacings. dimension_across_supports says which sheet dimension runs across the studs, furring or joists.

consumption_rates.condition: When the finish level requires it

consumption_rates.note: Rate comes from the specification, typically 2.0 to 3.0 kg per m2 depending on grain size
Rate by longest tile side, see tile_adhesive_rates and TF-04

Tiles, large format with any side 900 mm or more
